text:
maya: quick heads-up — starting the py/ts SDK 2.4.0 canary rollout now but CI hit a signing mismatch on npm, holding the publish.
jason: what mismatch? paste the log plz
ci-bot: npm publish failed: E403 Unauthorized - signing key mismatch (key-id=kp_2026_ROTATED). Registry rejected signature.
maya: exact error from the NPM step ^
alicia: hmm, that looks like the new key didn't propagate to the build agents. We rotated KMS last night. Who owns the rotation rollout?
rachel: that was me, but I only pushed the key to dedicated infra, not the transient builders. my bad — can push the rotated key to builders now.
tom: do we want to unblock with a manual override or freeze the rollout until keys are fixed? Risk: partial publish can create mismatched artifacts (npm succeeds later, pypi already uploaded).
sam: pypi step actually passed earlier for the same pipeline, so we could end up with Py package v2.4.0 and no npm package — bad state.
maya: agreed. let's halt everything. plan A: pin public SDK references to 2.3.12 in the temp docs and repo links until we can do a clean republish. Plan B: fix key propagation & re-run publish in a controlled canary window.
jason: rollback criteria we should agree on now so oncall knows when to stop the rollout if something slips:
- abort if >1% client install failures reported in first 30m
- abort if SDK api-error rate >0.5% above baseline in canary routes
- abort if publish shows divergent artifact sets across registries (npm vs pypi)
alicia: adding one more: abort if any checksum mismatch detected between our release manifest and registry artifacts.
rachel: timeline: I can push keys to builders in 30m. want to schedule republish in the 10:00-11:00 PT change window tomorrow to avoid disrupting evenings.
maya: good. owner for republish flow = rachel. owner for customer comms/deprecation blurb = alicia.
ci-bot: deploy-bot paused pipeline #sdk-publish/457 — action required: manual resume after key fix. (react :pause_button:)
deploy-bot: canary publish halted at step "npm:sign"
sam: action items:
1) rachel propagate key to builders + run a dry publish to staging (no public tag)
2) run smoke tests from staging npm/pypi installs (tom)
3) if clean, republish 2.4.0 during change window and then cut 2.4.1 hotfix if any post-publish fixes needed (maya)
4) docs + deprecation note prep (alicia)

rachel: starting key push to builders now. will report back in ~20m.

--- 18 minutes later ---

rachel: pushed keys and triggered a staging dry-run: `./scripts/publish-staging --tag staging --skip-cd` output attached.
tom: staging install ok for npm and pypi. smoke tests passed (basic runtime + async client tests) ~6/6.
jason: can we add an automated sanity check to the pipeline to verify registry parity before tagging public publish? e.g., publish to staging then check artifact hashes across registries.
maya: yes. add a gating step: post-publish check that compares manifest checksums. If mismatch, mark pipeline FAILED and do not create `latest`/`@latest` tags.
alicia: drafting release notes and the deprecation blurb — we'll deprecate "legacy sync client" in favor of new async-first API, announce migration guide and a 60-day deprecation window. putting PR up: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/release-2.4.0-notes
sam: publishing strategy: staggered canary = 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows; canary controlled by deploy-bot feature flags.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for tag `v2.4.0-canary` at 2026-04-02T17:00:00Z (hold). To resume: `@deploy-bot resume sdk-publish/457` after manual confirmation.

rachel: will re-run public publish in tomorrow's window. if anything fails, we push a revert tag `v2.4.0-revert` and reapply `v2.3.12` pin in docs.
maya: decision: hold public `latest` tag until we verify registry parity and sign keys. If dry-run and staging checks pass, proceed with staggered canary tomorrow. If any parity failure, abort and schedule 2.4.1 to fix the issue.
alicia: customer comms plan: short note explaining delayed publish due to signing rotation; include timeline and migration steps. will queue an internal FYI and external delay notice if publish slips more than 24 hours.
jason: add monitoring runbooks to the canary playbook (who pages on high install failures, run query for checksum mismatch, how to force revert tag). I'm adding a minimal script: 
```
# check parity
curl -sS https://registry.npmjs.org/@redwood/sdk/v2.4.0 | jq -r '.versions["2.4.0"].dist.shasum'
curl -sS https://pypi.org/pypi/redwood-sdk/2.4.0/json | jq -r '.urls[0].digests.sha256'
# compare hashes (transform npm shasum to sha256 mapping via our manifest)
```

sam: ok. final checklist for tomorrow's change window 10:00-11:00 PT:
- rachel: public key confirmed on builders + dry-run green
- tom: staging smoke tests green
- jason: parity gating step in pipeline
- alicia: release notes + deprecation notice ready
- maya: oncall coverage + rollout monitors configured

rachel: noted. I'll mark myself as owner and update the PR when done.
maya: thanks all. emojis for visibility :eyes: :rocket:

--- thread end ---
